summary: The paper introduces DIRECTER, an inference-time activation-steering method that scales KV-cache keys of instruction tokens and modulates steering strength via a plausibility-guided decoding loop and an attention-sensitivity layer ranking. The core idea—adaptively weakening steering when the steered top token is implausible under the raw distribution—is sensible, practical, and well-motivated by the oversteering problem, and the paper includes a reasonable spread of benchmarks, model scales, ablations, and efficiency/quality analyses. However, the gains are modest and inconsistent (DIRECTER is not the best method on the 3B and 7B models in Table 2, and only +0.3 over zero-shot at 1B), there is no statistical-significance treatment, the evaluation relies on a self-designed benchmark and a gpt-4o-mini-rewritten IFEval, and several justifications are deferred entirely to appendices. Novelty is moderate: the plausibility gate is adapted from contrastive/DoLa-style decoding and combined with KV steering.
strengths: Addresses a genuine and well-articulated problem (oversteering) with a dynamic, per-step control mechanism rather than static hyperparameters, and requires no extra profiling dataset unlike PASTA.
Good ablation coverage isolating the key design choices: fixed vs. adaptive strength, reversed ranking, random layers, and random-token steering, several with reported standard deviations.

Practical framing: efficiency analysis (throughput, per-token latency, memory), a gating shortcut to skip unnecessary steered passes, and compatibility with FlashAttention are concrete advantages over attention-level interventions.
The plausibility filter is shown to be modular—it improves PASTA and SpotLight when added as a safety gate—supporting the generality claim for that component.
Generation-quality and task-fidelity evaluation (LLM-judge plus a corroborating human eval in the appendix) directly probes the claimed no-trade-off property.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical soundness is weak. Results use greedy decoding (deterministic), but there is no significance testing and most main numbers are single runs; several improvements are small (e.g., 1B: 61.3→61.6; 14B differences of ~1-2 points), making it unclear whether the wins are real.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report variance across multiple prompt rewrites/paraphrases or bootstrap confidence intervals over benchmark items, and add significance tests (e.g., paired bootstrap) for the headline comparisons against tuned baselines.

key_concerns.issue: The generalization claim is overstated. Table 2 shows DIRECTER is NOT the best method on 3B (67.1 vs Few-shot 67.8) or 7B (74.4 vs SpotLight* 74.9), yet the text asserts a 'more robust, model-agnostic improvement.' This is a calibration problem.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Rescope the claim to 'consistently improves over zero-shot' (which the data support) and explicitly acknowledge where competing methods match or exceed DIRECTER, rather than implying uniform superiority.

key_concerns.issue: Evaluation setup raises confound/cherry-picking concerns: IFEval prompts are rewritten with gpt-4o-mini to separate instructions from tasks, and GSM8K-Format is a self-designed benchmark. Both deviate from standard protocols and could favor the proposed method, and neither can be cross-checked against literature numbers.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report results on unmodified IFEval alongside the rewritten version, and justify that the rewriting is applied identically and fairly to all baselines; provide inter-annotator/judge reliability for the new benchmark.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty is incremental: the plausibility constraint is essentially borrowed from contrastive-decoding/DoLa (cited Li et al. 2022; Chuang et al. 2023), and the contribution is its combination with KV-cache key scaling plus an ad hoc sensitivity metric that the authors themselves note lacks theoretical grounding.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Sharpen the delineation of what is genuinely new versus adapted, and either theoretically motivate the disturbance-score metric or empirically compare it against simpler layer-selection heuristics beyond random/reversed.

key_concerns.issue: Baseline breadth is limited to two attention-level steering methods (PASTA, SpotLight); residual-stream steering approaches (ITI/RepE/ActAdd-style) are discussed but not compared empirically.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one residual-stream steering baseline, or explicitly argue why such comparison is out of scope.

key_concerns.issue: Core justifications (metric formulation, why modulate L rather than α, key vs. value scaling) are deferred entirely to appendices not present here, so the main text alone under-supports central design decisions.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move at least a compact version of the metric justification and the L-vs-α argument into the main body.

questions_for_authors: On 3B and 7B (Table 2), DIRECTER underperforms Few-shot and SpotLight* respectively—can you explain why, and does this affect the 'model-agnostic' claim?
How do results change on the unmodified IFEval (without gpt-4o-mini rewriting), and is the rewriting applied identically to all baselines?
What is the variance/significance of the headline 6.5% and ~4% gains? Are they robust to prompt paraphrases and item-level bootstrapping?
How sensitive is the sensitivity-ranking (and thus performance) to the single-layer steering probe used to compute the disturbance score?
α=100 key scaling is large; can you characterize what this does mechanistically to attention mass after renormalization, and why performance saturates by α≈100?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly supported for the improve-over-zero-shot and no-quality-trade-off findings, but the 'robust, model-agnostic' generalization framing is overstated given DIRECTER is beaten by baselines at 3B/7B, and small gains lack significance testing.

significance.justification: A practical, dataset-free mechanism for mitigating oversteering that the steering subcommunity could adopt, though impact is bounded by modest gains.

novelty.justification: Combines a contrastive/DoLa-style plausibility gate with KV-cache key scaling and an ad hoc sensitivity ranking—useful but largely a recombination of existing ideas.

rigor.justification: Method is sound and controls (random layers/tokens, reversed ranking) are present, but some central design choices are justified only in absent appendices and the causal story for key scaling is thin.

statistical_soundness.justification: Greedy decoding gives determinism but there is no significance testing and mostly single-run numbers; several reported gains are small enough to plausibly be noise.

calibration_honesty.justification: A limitations section exists, but 'robust, model-agnostic improvement' overstates results that lose to baselines on 3B/7B; SOTA-style framing outruns the evidence.

clarity.justification: Method and algorithm are explained clearly overall, though the notation is dense and several key justifications are pushed to appendices.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure (abstract, intro, related work, method, experiments, conclusion, limitations) at appropriate length.

reproducibility.justification: Public models/benchmarks and key hyperparameters (α=100, β=0.5) are given, but a new benchmark, rewritten IFEval, and appendix-only details would complicate exact replication.

related_work.justification: Steering and instruction-following literature is fairly represented and the contribution is positioned against PASTA/SpotLight, though residual-stream steering is discussed but not compared empirically.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative, claim-supporting display items (ablations, robustness sweeps, efficiency), adequate for judging the evidence.

breadth_generality.justification: Multiple models (1B-14B) and three benchmarks, but only two steering baselines, a self-designed benchmark, and a modified IFEval limit support for the broad generality claimed.

overall_recommendation.justification: Competent, useful work with solid engineering but borderline due to modest/inconsistent gains, weak significance treatment, and evaluation-setup confounds.
